mcq.question: Angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 30 m away is 30°. Height of tower (ignore observer height):
Angle of depression is measured:
mcq.explanation: Depression — looking down; angle below horizontal.

assertion_reason.assertion: Angle of elevation of an object equals the angle of depression of the observer from the object.
assertion_reason.reason: They are alternate angles when horizontal lines through observer and object are parallel.
assertion_reason.explanation: Both true for standard setup with parallel horizontals.

vsa.question: A pole 10 m high casts a shadow 10 m long. Find the angle of elevation of the sun.
From the top of a 7 m building, angle of depression of a car is 45°. Find distance of car from building.

sa.question: Tower height is 50 m. Angle of elevation from a point on ground is 30°. Find distance from foot of tower.
A 1.5 m boy sees a tower at 60° elevation. He walks 30 m towards the tower to a point with 30° elevation. Find tower height.
sa.model_answer: Set up two equations with heights h and distances d, d−30; solve h = 15√3 m (standard NCERT type).

la.question: Student 1.5 m tall observes minar at 30° elevation from 28.5 m away. Find minar height.
From top of 80 m cliff, angles of depression of two boats in same line are 30° and 45°. Find distance between boats.
la.model_answer: Distances 80√3 and 80 m from cliff; difference = 80(√3 − 1) m.

la.question: Aeroplane flying 1 km high passes overhead with 60° elevation at one instant. Find horizontal distance after 15 s if speed is 720 km/h.
la.model_answer: Initial distance = 1/tan 60° = 1/√3 km; displacement in 15 s = 3 km; combine as required.
